definitions.explanation: Describes something changing so quickly or frequently that it is hard to keep up with. Often used for situations, environments, or pace of change.

examples.japanese: {目|め}まぐるしい{変化|へんか}。
{今日|きょう}は{目|め}まぐるしく{忙|いそが}しい{一日|いちにち}だった。
examples.english: Today was a hectically busy day.

examples.japanese: テクノロジーの{進歩|しんぽ}は{目|め}まぐるしく、{数年前|すうねんまえ}の{常識|じょうしき}がもう{通用|つうよう}しない。
examples.english: Technological progress is so rapid that common knowledge from just a few years ago no longer applies.

notes:
FORMS:
- Adnominal: {目|め}まぐるしい + noun
- Adverbial: {目|め}まぐるしく
- Predicate: {目|め}まぐるしい

USAGE:
The adverbial form {目|め}まぐるしく is very common. Often used with {変化|へんか} (change), {展開|てんかい} (development), or {動|うご}く (to move).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目|め}まぐるしい{変化|へんか}: dizzying change
- {目|め}まぐるしい{展開|てんかい}: rapid development
- {目|め}まぐるしく{変|か}わる: to change rapidly
- {目|め}まぐるしい{一日|いちにち}: a hectic day

ETYMOLOGY:
Related to {目|め}が{回|まわ}る (eyes spin, to feel dizzy). Conveys the sense of things moving so fast one can barely follow.

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {目|め}まぐるしくなかったら
